The Silent Soma

A well-fitted pyramidal neuron model fired beautifully on its home morphology, then fell quiet on a real reconstructed cell. Follow the signal to find out why.

Sadaf Mansuri · Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences / Computational Neuroscience Lab

👇 Click any node to travel along the pathway
Stage 1 · Build

Two parts, one virtual neuron

Biophysical models are usually fitted on one cell and reused on many. This project asks a simple question: does that reuse actually work?

Detailed neuron models are rarely checked for how well they transfer. Here a canonical electrical model was assigned to a new electron-microscopy cell on the Open Brain Institute Virtual Lab, and everything was tested.

Stage 2 · Fit

Teaching the model to spike like a real cell

Evolution does the work: 401 generations of MO-CMA search tuned 23 parameters against 110 recorded features.

Best score 70.323 free parameters110 target featuresNo dendritic active parameters
Plot twist. The somatic fast sodium conductance (NaTg) collapsed to its lower bound, zero. Spikes in this model can only start in the axon. Largest misfits: depolarization block (z≈6.9) and inverse time to first spike (z≈5.2).
Stage 3 · Fire

At home, the neuron fires happily

On its small soma + AIS placeholder, the model spikes repetitively from 130% to 300% of threshold.

Threshold 0.083 nAHolding −0.064 nARest −72.6 mVRin 111 MΩPeak ≈ +10 mV

The upstroke is carried by NaTg, then a Ca_LVAst phase; K_Tst and SKv3_1 repolarize, and Ih and passive currents dominate between spikes.

Stage 4 · Test

Eight validations on the MICrONS cell: 7 pass, 1 fails

Tap a card to read what happened in each validation. The model passes overall only if every test passes, so it fails.

Stage 5 · Explain

A soma with no sodium, buried in a big dendritic tree

The axon still spikes (up to +32 mV). The soma just cannot follow it any more.

PropertyHome (soma + AIS)MICrONS ME-model
Threshold current0.083 nA≈ 0.465 nA (5.6× higher)
Input resistance111 MΩ≈ 80 MΩ
Resting potential−72.6 mV≈ −78 mV
Somatic spikeFull, ≈ +10 mVSmall deflections on a plateau
Repetitive firingSustainedSpiking test failed
Hypothesis (untested). With no somatic sodium channels, the soma is driven only by current from the axonal spike. On the small placeholder that is enough. On MICrONS, a large passive arbor adds load and the axonal spike can no longer drive the soma.
Read the passes with care. I-V only needs a positive slope, and F-I and depolarization block passed despite a falling somatic spike count and a sustained plateau. Platform status is qualitative. The 1 ms axon-before-soma order is also built in, since the soma cannot fire first.
Stage 6 · Fix

Re-fit it, then trust it

A model that fails a validation should not be used to study firing, such as channelopathies or drug effects, until it is re-fitted or the failure is explained.

  1. Allow a somatic sodium conductance and repeat the validations.
  2. Re-optimize the E-model on the MICrONS morphology with its dendrites.
  3. Replace qualitative status with quantitative features compared to experimental ranges.
  4. Evaluate apical propagation and explain the spike at about 45 ms before stimulation.

Limitations: single ME-model and seed; values read by eye from figures; criteria known for 2 of 8 validations; no experimental comparison.
